newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends up on increased Iraq-Kurd tension.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends up on increased Iraq-Kurd tension.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended higher Wednesday, bucking declines in the rest of the oil complex, after an Iraqi Kurdish group said rival Kurds and Iraqi forces were preparing for a possible attack against it.

"It may have some sort of basis in fact, but whether it leads to anything unusual in Iraq and affects (oil) supply is another story," said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Group in New York.
"The market decided it's worth a little more than 10 cents, and that seems about right," said Evans.
April crude settled up 11 cents at $21.11 a barrel.

The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) said there were signs of an imminent attack by the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the troops of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein on the PUK stronghold, Sulaimaniya province in northern Iraq.
"There is nothing new. I do not believe there is any basis for these accusations," a KDP spokesman told Reuters.

Iraq has an agreement with the United Nations to export oil in exchange for humanitarian aid. The PUK's statements created concern that a possible attack by Iraqi troops on the PUK could suspend the pact and tighten crude supply.

March heating oil ended off 0.14 cent a gallon at 56.68 cents. March gasoline ended up a mere 0.03 cent at 62.26 cents a gallon, erasing an early session rally which pushed it up 1.37 cents to 63.60 cents.

On Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported in its oil inventory data that gasoline stocks unexpectedly declined 3.2 million barrels for the week ended February 21 due to a surprise increase in demand.

"It seems that the market jumped the gun on gasoline. It's too early for a spring rally," said a New York dealer. Gasoline traditionally rallys in the spring in anticipation of the summer driving season when demand typically peaks.
Traders had been expecting the API data to show a slight build in gasoline stocks, reflecting February's usual lacklustre demand.
The April/May gasoline spread, however, remained firm as dealers turned to April gasoline plays ahead of the March contract expiry in refined products on Friday.
Meanwhile, heating oil was weak as mild temperatures continue to bathe the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
The mild weather has created a year-over-year surplus of 1.85 million barrels in the region, the first heating oil surplus there since December 1995, the API said.
The National Weather Service's six-to-10 day forecast starting March 2 called for above normal temperatures for the Northeast.

Oil prices have been in a seasonal downtrend in the last several weeks. Crude and heating oil prices have declined about 20 percent since January, and dealers expect prices to spike lower again before the gasoline rally begins in March.
"We could go near $20.00 before rising again," said a New York crude dealer. The seven-month low for prompt crude is $20.65 made on Monday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
